member.name: T:HumanGateway.Security.AuthenticatedUser
member.summary: The authenticated user resolved from a valid session token (AUTH-FR-02, SP-03). Carries just enough identity for the service layer to authorise requests: the user id (referenced from participant.userId), the username, and a display name. HumanGateway performs no role-checking here (SP-09) — per-conversation/task/artifact authorisation is enforced by the authorisation middleware against conversation membership (AUTH-FR-03).

member.name: T:HumanGateway.Security.PasswordHasher
member.summary: PHC-string password hashing for local/remote user credentials (user.schema.json#/passwordVerifier, AUTH-FR-02, SP-07). v1 uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with a per-hash random salt, encoded as a PHC string: $pbkdf2-sha256$i=<iterations>,l=<bytes>$<base64 salt>$<base64 hash>.
member.remarks: The PHC format keeps the verifier self-describing (algorithm, cost, salt, digest) so future rounds can raise the cost and re-verify old hashes — no per-site migration needed. Salt and digest are standard base64 (schema pattern ^\$[A-Za-z0-9+./=,$-]{19,511}$). The verifier is a local-store-only field: it is hashed with a cost parameter (default , OWASP-recommended for PBKDF2-SHA256) and is never transmitted in any protocol payload and never logged (SP-07).

member.summary: Default PBKDF2-SHA256 cost (OWASP recommendation).

member.summary: Salt length in bytes (128 bits).

member.summary: Digest length in bytes (256 bits, matching SHA-256).

member.name: F:HumanGateway.Security.PasswordHasher.Algorithm
member.summary: Algorithm token used in the PHC string.

member.name: M:HumanGateway.Security.PasswordHasher.PhcRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^\\$pbkdf2-sha256\\$i=([0-9]+),l=([0-9]+)\\$([A-Za-z0-9+/=]+)\\$([A-Za-z0-9+/=]+)$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match the string "$pbkdf2-sha256$i=".
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9] atomically at least once.
○ Match the string ",l=".
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9] atomically at least once.
○ Match '$'.
○ 3rd capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [+/-9=A-Za-z] atomically at least once.
○ Match '$'.
○ 4th capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [+/-9=A-Za-z] atomically at least once.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:HumanGateway.Security.PasswordHasher.Hash(System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: Hashes into a PHC string. The salt is drawn from a cryptographic RNG; identical passwords never produce the same verifier.

member.name: M:HumanGateway.Security.PasswordHasher.Verify(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Verifies against a PHC verifier. The stored algorithm/cost/salt drive the recomputation, so any previously-issued verifier stays valid; the digest comparison is constant-time.

member.summary: ASP.NET middleware that authenticates requests carrying an Authorization: Bearer <token> session token (AUTH-FR-02, SP-03). When a well-formed bearer token is present and valid, the resolved is exposed via under . Requests without a token pass through unauthenticated — enforcing a required session is the caller's choice (the authorisation middleware, AUTH-FR-03). An invalid or expired token is rejected with 401 so a broken client cannot silently fall back to anonymous.

member.name: T:HumanGateway.Security.SessionTokens
member.summary: Session-token primitives for authenticated users (AUTH-FR-02, SP-03). A session token is an opaque, high-entropy bearer credential (hgsu_ + 256 bits of base64url randomness) issued to a user after a successful login. Following the gateway registration-token pattern (identity-security Open Q #1: signed opaque/session tokens v1; JWT only if a consumer needs it), the service stores only the SHA-256 fingerprint of the token in its sessions table — never the plaintext token (SP-07). Verification is a constant-time fingerprint comparison so a timing side-channel cannot leak token bytes.

member.name: F:HumanGateway.Security.SessionTokens.TokenBodyPattern
member.summary: The token body after the prefix: 43..251 chars of base64url. Combined with the 5-char prefix this yields a 48..256-char token, matching the gateway schema's requestToken bounds.

member.name: M:HumanGateway.Security.SessionTokens.TokenShapeRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^hgsu_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43,251}$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match the string "hgsu_".
○ Match a character in the set [\-0-9A-Z_a-z] atomically at least 43 and at most 251 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.
